prompt.alinti: How do we make environments like this for our game, despite both being terrible at 3D modeling?
The secret is a technique called projection.
Our artist starts by drawing every asset on an isometric grid that matches the camera angle in our game.
We then project those drawings onto simple 3D meshes.
Once everything's laid out in the level, we add a few extra layers to bring the environment to life.
We add decals to break up the walls and floors and stop the environment from feeling too repetitive.
For light sources, we use hand-drawn animated flipbooks to keep them consistent with the illustrated style.
Then we use lighting and post-processing to create depth and really sell the illusion that everything's 3D.
This process lets us build stylized environments surprisingly quickly, even though we're only a team of two and neither of us knows how to properly model anything.
